missing.item: Show a concrete loss beyond the intended slashing of pre-withdrawal misconduct.
missing.why: The report shows a slash can finalize after unstaking and deregistration, but does not identify a victim or establish that the slashed assets were not intended to remain slashable under the withdrawal-delay design.
missing.resolves_when: Identify the affected vault and party, the amount lost, and why those funds were not intended to be subject to this slash.

missing.item: Resolve whether the registration invariant must hold at slashing finalization despite a request made during the withdrawal delay.
missing.why: The report cites the registration invariant, while the policy context also describes the withdrawal delay as allowing the DSS to slash before withdrawal. Whether this queued-slash sequence is excluded or violates the invariant remains unclear.
missing.resolves_when: Cite policy language establishing that registration must persist through finalization, or otherwise establish that this sequence is intended to be disallowed.

missing.item: Provide a compiling, passing reproduction test.
missing.why: The source supports the request, unstake, deregister, and finalize sequence, but the supplied test is not shown to compile or run.
missing.resolves_when: Provide a test that compiles and passes against the audited commit.

reason: Scope references and the source-supported path are resolved: the report describes a reachable queued slash finalized after deregistration. The distinct harm and the policy treatment of that sequence remain unresolved.

evidence.claim: A DSS can finalize a slashing against an operator after the operator has unstaked its vaults and unregistered from that DSS, violating the invariant 'Only DSSs an operator is registered with can slash said operator'.
evidence.support_reason: requestSlashing (Core.sol:220-231) checks registration only at request time and stores the queued slashing root in self.slashingRequests (SlasherLib.sol:110). finalizeSlashing (SlasherLib.sol:126-151) only checks the stored root and the veto window; it never re-checks isOperatorRegisteredToDSS or that the vaults are still staked to the DSS. unregisterOperatorFromDSS (Operator.sol:181-203) only requires vaultStakedInDssMap[dss] to be empty, which unstaking satisfies, and does not consult pending slashing requests. So the sequence request -> unstake -> unregister -> finalize is reachable.
preconditions: operator registered to DSS with >=1 vault staked
operator unstakes all vaults (9-day MIN_STAKE_UPDATE_DELAY) and unregisters before the 2-day SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW elapses
DSS requested slashing before the unstake finalized

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the slash actually transfers value from a vault the operator no longer has staked to the DSS, and that this is a loss to anyone (stakers/DSS) rather than the intended 'slash for pre-withdrawal misbehavior'
missing_evidence.why: The stated impact is 'potential loss on deposits' and 'new users depositing into the DSS may be unaware'. The code shows the slash is applied to the vault's totalAssets (SlasherLib.sol:135-138, Vault.sol:193-205), which is the same effect as a normal in-window slash. Without showing a concrete victim whose funds are lost (e.g., a staker who deposited after the request, or a vault that was legitimately unstaked), the effect does not establish a distinct harm beyond the documented withdrawal-delay design.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A concrete scenario is given where a specific party loses funds that the protocol design did not intend to be slashable, with the amounts and the vault/staker identified.

missing_evidence.item: Reconciliation with the contest policy statement that the withdrawal delay exists precisely so the DSS can slash the vault before withdrawal, and that 'sitting on a queued withdraw doesn't provide an operator any edge'
missing_evidence.why: The policy explicitly frames the 9-day delay as the window in which the DSS may slash. The report's scenario is a slash requested inside that window and finalized after unstaking; if the policy treats this as intended behavior, the finding is excluded. The report must show the invariant is meant to bind at finalize time, not just at request time.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The report cites a policy clause or sponsor statement establishing that the registration check must hold at finalize time, or the judge confirms the invariant applies to finalization.

missing_evidence.item: The PoC test is not shown to compile/run (it references helpers stake_vaults_to_dss, dss, operator, and calls finalizeUpdateVaultStakeInDSS with a queued struct that must match the stored root)
missing_evidence.why: The code path is clear from source reading alone; a runnable test would confirm it but its absence does not undermine the reachability shown by the source.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A test is provided that compiles and passes against the audited commit.
